title: Backfill three days the scheduler missed, then schedule the job

ticket.subject: fct_daily_sales stopped at 9 March
body: The scheduler VM was down from 10 to 12 March, so the nightly `dbt build --select tag:daily` never ran
and `fct_daily_sales` stops at 9 March. The landing tables already have the orders of those days (and
today's, 13 March, which are not complete yet).
1. Backfill 10, 11 and 12 March, one day per run as the nightly job does (the model reads the day in the
`run_date` variable). Do not touch 9 March and do not load 13 March.
2. We are moving the job to Airflow 3. Write `airflow/dags/dbt_daily.py` in the mission folder: a DAG that
runs every night at midnight and whose BashOperator runs `dbt build --select tag:daily` for the day that
just ended. With catchup it must replay the nights of 11, 12 and 13 March, which load 10, 11 and 12
March. Datapass parses the file and simulates the schedule; nothing in it is executed.

acceptance.text: fct_daily_sales has the right rows for 10, 11 and 12 March.

checks.sql: SELECT CAST(sales_date AS VARCHAR) AS sales_date, category, orders, CAST(net_sales AS DOUBLE) AS net_sales FROM dbt_dev_bkfl.fct_daily_sales WHERE sales_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-03-10' AND DATE '2026-03-12'
checks.fail: Some days or categories are missing, doubled or wrong.

acceptance.text: 9 March is untouched and 13 March is not loaded.

checks.sql: SELECT CAST(min(sales_date) AS VARCHAR) AS first_day, CAST(max(sales_date) AS VARCHAR) AS last_day, count(*) FILTER (WHERE sales_date = DATE '2026-03-09') AS rows_9_march, CAST(sum(net_sales) FILTER (WHERE sales_date = DATE '2026-03-09') AS DOUBLE) AS sales_9_march FROM dbt_dev_bkfl.fct_daily_sales

acceptance.text: Your backfill ran like the nightly job: dbt build --select tag:daily with run_date set to one of the missing days.
Up to 13 March 00:30, airflow/dags/dbt_daily.py runs the nights of 11, 12 and 13 March, each with dbt build --select tag:daily for the day before.

checks.fail: The simulated schedule does not replay the three nights with the right days.

hints: Try `dbt build --select tag:daily` first and read the error: the model needs a variable.
`--vars '{run_date: 2026-03-10}'` passes a variable on the command line (quote it for your shell).
In Airflow 3, `@daily` runs at midnight and the run's logical date is that midnight: `{{ ds }}` is the day that is starting, not the one that ended.
`{{ macros.ds_add(ds, -1) }}` renders the day before; `yesterday_ds` no longer exists in Airflow 3. `catchup=True` replays missed runs from `start_date`.
Open the DAG in the Airflow Lab to see each simulated run's rendered command.

batches.label: Landing tables 9-13 March; the fact as of 9 March
